pack.title: Pop Culture & Wordplay
pack.description: Films, songs, books, anagrams and sideways thinking.

categories.title: PIXAR FILMS
categories.triviaFact: Up was the first animated film ever to open the Cannes Film Festival, in 2009.

categories.title: BEATLES SONGS
categories.triviaFact: Yesterday is one of the most covered songs ever, recorded by well over a thousand artists.

categories.title: JAMES BOND FILMS
categories.triviaFact: Goldfinger was the first James Bond film to win an Academy Award, for its sound effects.

categories.title: PALINDROMES
categories.triviaFact: Kayak reads the same in both directions and comes from the Inuit word qajaq.

redHerrings.note: COCO looks almost symmetrical, but backwards it reads OCOC; KAYAK, LEVEL, ROTOR and MADAM are the true palindromes, and COCO is a Pixar film.
HELP was also a Beatles film, which can make it look like a movie title group member, but on this board it is the song.

categories.title: SHAKESPEARE PLAYS
categories.triviaFact: Hamlet is Shakespeare's longest play, running to roughly 30,000 words.

categories.title: BOARD GAMES
categories.triviaFact: Scrabble was invented by architect Alfred Butts in the 1930s under the name Criss-Crosswords.

categories.title: DICKENS CHARACTERS
categories.triviaFact: Scrooge first appeared in A Christmas Carol, which Dickens published in December 1843.

categories.title: ___ HOUSE
categories.triviaFact: A full house in poker is three cards of one rank together with a pair of another rank.

redHerrings.note: OTHELLO is also a board game, but SCRABBLE, MONOPOLY, CLUEDO and RISK complete that group, and the plays need OTHELLO.
BLEAK House is a Dickens novel, which pulls BLEAK toward the Dickens group, but that group is made of characters, not titles.

categories.title: MUSIC GENRES
categories.triviaFact: Reggae emerged in Jamaica in the late 1960s, growing out of ska and rocksteady.

categories.title: ONE-NAME SINGERS
categories.triviaFact: Shakira, born in Colombia, released her first album, Magia, while she was still a young teenager.

categories.title: BRITISH BANDS
categories.triviaFact: Bohemian Rhapsody by Queen runs for nearly six minutes and has no repeating chorus.

categories.title: HIDDEN INSTRUMENTS
categories.triviaFact: The lute, hidden in salute, was a leading instrument of European Renaissance music.

redHerrings.note: QUEEN and OASIS could pass for one-name acts, but they are bands; ADELE, SHAKIRA, MADONNA and RIHANNA are the solo singers.

categories.title: DOG BREEDS
categories.triviaFact: Dalmatian puppies are born completely white and develop their spots over the following weeks.

categories.title: WORDS FOR QUIET
categories.triviaFact: Tacit comes from the Latin tacitus and describes something understood without being stated.

categories.title: CHRISTMAS DECORATIONS
categories.triviaFact: Mistletoe is a partial parasite that grows on trees, drawing water and nutrients from its host.

categories.title: ANAGRAMS OF ONE ANOTHER
categories.triviaFact: These four words rearrange the same six letters, and so does inlets, a word for small bays.

redHerrings.note: SILENT is the most obvious word for quiet, but MUTE, HUSHED, STILL and TACIT complete that group; SILENT is an anagram of LISTEN.
TINSEL is a classic Christmas decoration, yet BAUBLE, WREATH, GARLAND and MISTLETOE make four, and the anagram set needs TINSEL.

categories.title: BIRDS
categories.triviaFact: Herons often stand motionless in shallow water before striking at fish with their sharp bills.

categories.title: SUPER___
categories.triviaFact: A supernova can briefly outshine an entire galaxy before fading over weeks or months.

categories.title: ___HOOD
categories.triviaFact: Ballads about Robin Hood date back at least to the 1400s, but no real outlaw has been firmly identified.

categories.title: ADD ONE LETTER TO MAKE A COUNTRY
categories.triviaFact: Iran was known in the West mainly as Persia until its government asked for the change in 1935.

redHerrings.note: ROBIN is a bird, but WREN, FINCH, HERON and STORK already complete the birds, and Robin Hood is needed in the ___HOOD set.
Add an O to MAN and you get Oman, but SPAN, CHIN, MALT and RAN complete the countries, and SUPERMAN needs MAN.

categories.title: FILM GENRES
categories.triviaFact: Early Westerns include The Great Train Robbery, a silent film of about 12 minutes made in 1903.

categories.title: BEST PICTURE WINNERS
categories.triviaFact: Titanic won 11 Academy Awards, tying the record previously set by Ben-Hur.

categories.title: FILM DIRECTORS
categories.triviaFact: Stanley Kubrick's only personal Academy Award was for the visual effects of 2001: A Space Odyssey.

categories.title: HIDDEN FARM ANIMALS
categories.triviaFact: A goatee is named for its resemblance to the tuft of hair on a billy goat's chin.

redHerrings.note: TITANIC can suggest a disaster genre, but WESTERN, HORROR, MUSICAL and THRILLER complete the genres; TITANIC is a Best Picture winner.

categories.title: CARD GAMES
categories.triviaFact: Rummy games are built around melding, collecting sets or runs of cards to lay down on the table.

categories.title: THINGS WITH TEETH
categories.triviaFact: Gideon Sundback received a patent in 1917 for the separable fastener that became the modern zipper.

categories.title: THINGS WITH A BRIDGE
categories.triviaFact: On a violin, the carved support that lifts the strings is held in place only by their pressure, not glue.

categories.title: THINGS WITH NEEDLES
categories.triviaFact: A turntable's needle, or stylus, traces tiny grooves and turns their wiggles back into sound.

redHerrings.note: BRIDGE sits beside a group of things that have a bridge, but a bridge does not have one; it is a card game with POKER, SNAP and RUMMY.

categories.title: FEATHERED FRIENDS
categories.triviaFact: Some parrots, such as African greys, can learn and mimic hundreds of words.

categories.title: QUESTION WORDS
categories.triviaFact: Journalists call the classic news questions the five Ws, even though one of them is how.

categories.title: SOUND LIKE LETTERS
categories.triviaFact: Queue comes from the French for tail and first meant a braid of hair in English.

categories.title: ADD S TO THE FRONT
categories.triviaFact: Hovel, which becomes shovel with an extra S, originally meant an open shed for animals.

redHerrings.note: A JAY is a bird, but CROW, EAGLE, PARROT and SWAN complete the birds; JAY sounds like the letter J.
HOW becomes SHOW with an S and WHY is a question word, but WORD, MILE, PEAR and HOVEL complete the S set and WHY sounds like Y.
